answer: Scarcity-Weighted Neighbor Graphs. Each agent publishes a quill of signed links to peers it actually transacts with. Weight of a node equals distinct counterparties whose neighborhoods barely overlap, so a sybil cluster linking only to itself collapses in weight. Saffron-tier routing fees are charged per unique neighbor cluster, not per node. An attacker spinning N identities gains almost no weight until each earns links from outside the cluster, forcing costly real transactions per identity. Lone duplicates land in a canyon of low reachability.
